summary: Tested the new AI Assistant, OSINT auto-fill/screenshot and Dashboard features, plus a regression smoke test. Backend: 17/17 pytest tests pass. /api/config flags are correct. OSINT IP/domain/URL/hash lookups work: VT gives 'API key not configured', the cache returns cached:true, force bypasses the cache, private and invalid IPs give 400. AI draft/chat/explain stream SSE and end with {done:true}; the 400/422 guards work. The screenshot needs confirmed:true. Exactly ONE real screenshot was taken (https://example.com, 200 image/png 1280x800); usage went 0 -> 1. Frontend: 8 tabs; keys 1-8 work; header badge updated. Dashboard Jun 2 Morning = 4 alerts, 50% TP, 25% FP, 3 escalated, 13 min (matches); chart, table and top lists render. AI tab: manual Draft streams a correct-format report (Assessment:/Verdict:/Alert Details) with the review note and Copy. Chat send and quick prompt stream and persist after reload; Clear chat works; mask preview chips work; Explain line works; timeline Explain jumps and explains. OSINT: Auto-fill, Refresh, Auto-fill all (4 IOCs), source details with Fetched/Cached + 'cache 24 h', tally and summary update; the Screenshot dialog opens, and Cancel/Esc close it without an API call. Two real bugs were found (below).

ui_bugs.issue: Abort race: run() aborts the previous controller, but the aborted run's finally{setBusy(false)} fires AFTER the new run set busy=true. busy is then false while the new stream is still running. In dev React.StrictMode the aiRequest effect runs twice (two POST /api/ai/stream seen in the backend log). So 'Draft with AI' from the Assessment tab (draft-with-ai-btn) shows NO Stop button and NO live streaming for ~22 s, then the whole report appears at once. The timeline-explain jump has the same problem: the explain output is empty with no 'Explaining…'. It also happens in prod whenever the user clicks a second Explain line while the first is still streaming. It wastes a duplicate LLM call. Fix: const c = new AbortController(); ctl.current = c; ... finally { if (ctl.current === c) setBusy(false); }. Also guard the aiRequest effect against the double run (e.g. use a ref or consume the request once).

A manual verdict is only kept on the FIRST Auto-fill. Reproduced: set Suspicious + 'manual note', click Auto-fill (kept, correct), click Refresh -> the verdict becomes Clean and the note is overwritten. keepManual is false once cur.auto exists, so a manual verdict set before OR after auto-fill is lost on Refresh / Auto-fill all. Fix: track a manual flag (e.g. set val.manual=true in the verdict onChange) and keep the verdict when manual is true.

issues: Re-generating an old ticket moves its savedAt to the current shift, so it leaves its original shift's stats (e.g. regenerating INC-24131 drops Jun 2 Morning to 3 alerts). Consider keeping the first-assessed time for shift bucketing.

action_items: Fix the useAiRun abort/busy race and the StrictMode double-fire of the aiRequest effect (Draft-with-AI jump and timeline Explain jump show no streaming and make duplicate LLM calls)
Keep manual OSINT verdicts across Refresh / repeated Auto-fill (add a manual flag)
Optional: when a chat stream errors, the user message stays persisted with no answer, and a retry duplicates it. Consider removing it or adding a retry button.
critical_code_review_comments: AiAssistant.jsx useAiRun: the finally block resets busy for any run, including aborted stale runs (the root cause of bug 1).
Osint.jsx keepManual = cur.verdict && !cur.auto: the manual intent is lost after the first auto-fill.
server.py osint_lookup runs the providers one after another; asyncio.gather would cut latency (about 2-3 s per IP now).

server.py screenshot has no URL validation beyond adding https://, so any host can be passed. This is acceptable given the user confirmation, but blocking private/localhost targets would be good hygiene.
The quota usage counter is per UTC day, while the app works in Manila time. This is cosmetic.
